work.title: Selected work
work.subtitle: Real systems, real outcomes - framed by the business impact they delivered.

items.title: Scaling SolarSquare's ERP to 450+ users
items.challenge: A growing solar business needed its ERP to reliably support hundreds of concurrent users across finance, supply chain, and warehouse operations - without downtime as load scaled.
items.approach: As the solo engineer leading the ERP function, I re-architected ERPNext into a horizontally scaled, cloud-native platform on AWS: an auto-scaling web tier (Gunicorn/Nginx/SocketIO), a dedicated worker fleet, ElastiCache Redis, RDS MariaDB, S3, and Lambda - with CloudWatch and IAM for operations and security.
items.outcome: Enterprise-grade performance and elasticity for 450+ users across B2B and B2C, on infrastructure that scales with demand.

items.title: Preventing ~₹20 Lakh in logistics losses
items.challenge: Inventory was leaking value in mid-mile logistics, with no clear visibility into where or why losses occurred.
items.approach: I built inventory-tracking workflows and data pipelines that surfaced discrepancies as they happened, giving operations the transparency to act before losses compounded.
items.outcome: Identified and prevented roughly ₹20 Lakh in mid-mile logistics losses, with measurably better warehouse efficiency and operational transparency.

items.title: Audit & IPO readiness (ITGC)
items.challenge: Preparing for IPO scrutiny meant the ERP had to demonstrate strong IT General Controls over access, change, and operations.
items.approach: I built a custom RBAC framework with end-to-end activity logging, implemented maker-checker approval workflows enforcing segregation of duties on sensitive financial transactions, and developed an audit framework that captures access, change, and approval evidence into structured reports.
items.outcome: An ERP posture that directly addresses the access, change, and operations control domains expected in SOX and ITGC audits.

items.title: ERPNext core contribution - PR #51644
items.challenge: ERPNext's stock-ledger serial-number resolution was slow on large, serial-tracked inventories - affecting Delivery Note, Purchase Receipt, Stock Entry, and Stock Reconciliation across the global community.
items.approach: I refactored get_stock_ledgers_for_serial_nos onto ERPNext v15's Serial and Batch Bundle data model, replacing application-layer filtering with bundle-based SQL joins while preserving backward compatibility with legacy serial data.
items.outcome: Query execution dropped from ~583s to ~67s (~8.7× faster) and database queries from ~104K to ~14.5K (~86% fewer) - merged into the world's leading open-source ERP (34K+ GitHub stars).

items.title: Event-management ERP for Amba Tech (NGO)
items.challenge: An NGO needed an end-to-end system to run events - registrations, attendance, and decision-making - without enterprise budgets.
items.approach: I designed and built a full ERP with an Angular web app, a mobile app, and Metabase dashboards, including a QR-based attendance system for precise tracking and Frappe API integrations for clean data flow.
items.outcome: Data-driven event operations for the organizing team, with accurate attendance tracking and dashboards that informed planning.

about.title: About
paragraphs: I'm a senior software engineer with 4+ years of experience designing, building, and operating production-grade ERP and data systems on AWS. Today I lead the ERP function at **SolarSquare**, single-handedly running a horizontally scaled ERPNext platform for 450+ users across finance, supply chain, and warehouse operations.

My background spans distributed systems, backend integrations, observability, and IT General Controls (ITGC) for audit and IPO readiness. I like working close to the business - turning ambiguous operational problems into reliable systems with measurable impact.
